functions.sig: (game: int, root: str | Path | None = None) -> MetricaMatch
functions.doc: Metrica sample game 1 or 2: tracking of both teams, ball and events in metres (downloaded once, ~65 MB).

functions.name: skillcorner_matches
functions.sig: (root: str | Path | None = None) -> list[dict]
functions.doc: The ten SkillCorner open-data matches (``id``, teams, date).

functions.name: skillcorner_ball
functions.sig: (match_id: int, root: str | Path | None = None) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]
functions.doc:
Ball track of a SkillCorner match at 10 Hz: ``frame, t, period, x, y, z, detected`` (NaN when missing).

The ~90 MB JSON-lines tracking file is downloaded once and reduced to a small ``.npz``; the raw file is kept
only if ``keep_raw`` is set in the environment (``PINNEAPPLE_KEEP_RAW=1``).

functions.name: statsbomb_shots
functions.sig: (seasons: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] | None = None, root: str | Path | None = None, *, max_matches: int | None = None) -> list[dict]
functions.doc:
Every open-play and set-piece shot with a 360 freeze frame in the given StatsBomb seasons.

Each shot: ``match_id, season, x, y`` (StatsBomb yards, 120 x 80, attacking towards x = 120), ``goal`` (0/1),
``body_part, shot_type, technique, first_time, under_pressure, statsbomb_xg`` and ``freeze`` (list of
``(x, y, teammate, keeper)`` of the players visible in the 360 frame). The reduced table is cached as
``statsbomb/shots_<season>.json.gz`` so the ~3 GB of raw match files are read only once.

children.name: pinneapple_systems.sports.football.kin_study
children.doc:
Player-kinematics studies: smoothing with known truth, processing uncertainty of metabolic power on real
tracking, and trajectory prediction with and without physical limits at equal data.

* :func:`synthetic_smoothing` -- simulated runs (bounded speed and acceleration) observed with noise: error of
  speed, acceleration and metabolic power per method (raw differences, Savitzky-Golay, Kalman-RTS) and the
  coverage of the Kalman 95 % intervals.
* :func:`match_load` -- one Metrica match: noise level by maximum likelihood, plausibility per method, metabolic
  power per player per method (the spread is the processing uncertainty).
* :func:`prediction_samples` / :func:`prediction_study` -- position of every outfield player 1 s or 2 s ahead
  from his past second: constant velocity, decaying-acceleration physics, gradient-boosted trees on the history,
  trees on the residual of constant velocity, the same projected onto the reachable set; trained on one match and
  tested on the other with growing training sets.

functions.name: synthetic_runs
functions.sig: (n: int = 20, T: float = 60.0, fps: float = 25.0, *, seed: int = 0, v_cap: float = 9.0, a_cap: float = 6.0, tau: float = 1.0, sigma_a: float = 3.0)
functions.doc:
True positions, velocities and accelerations of ``n`` players: Ornstein-Uhlenbeck acceleration (time
constant ``tau``, stationary std ``sigma_a``) clipped at ``a_cap``, speed clipped at ``v_cap``.

functions.name: synthetic_smoothing
functions.sig: (noise = (0.05, 0.2), fps = (25.0, 10.0), *, n: int = 20, seed: int = 0) -> list[dict[str, Any]]
functions.doc: RMSE of speed, acceleration and metabolic power per smoothing method against the known truth.

functions.name: match_load
functions.sig: (match, *, team: str = 'Home', max_frames: int | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
Metabolic power of one team of a Metrica match per player and per method, and plausibility per method
(the first ``max_frames`` frames only, if given). ``gated_mean_mp_per_player`` drops the samples above the
human limits of :mod:`.kinematics` (tracking jumps), which otherwise dominate a match mean.

functions.name: prediction_samples
functions.sig: (match, horizon: float, *, every: float = 1.0, history: float = 1.0) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]
functions.doc:
Samples ``(features, pos, vel, acc, target)`` for every outfield player every ``every`` s with a complete
past ``history`` and a tracked position ``horizon`` s later. States are causal Kalman estimates.

functions.name: prediction_study
functions.sig: (train: dict, test: dict, horizon: float, *, sizes = (100, 300, 1000, 3000, None), seeds = (0, 1, 2)) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc: Final displacement error on ``test`` of each predictor trained on random subsets of ``train``.

children.summary: Player-kinematics studies: smoothing with known truth, processing uncertainty of metabolic power on real tracking, and trajectory prediction with and without physical limits at equal data.

children.name: pinneapple_systems.sports.football.kinematics
children.doc:
Player kinematics from tracking: smoothing with uncertainty, physical plausibility, metabolic power and
short-horizon trajectory prediction with and without physical limits.

* :func:`kalman_smooth` -- constant-acceleration (white-jerk) Kalman filter with a Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoother per
  coordinate, vectorised over players; positions, velocities and accelerations with their standard deviations.
  Missing samples (NaN) are bridged by the model.
* :func:`savgol_derivatives`, :func:`finite_differences` -- the usual data-only alternatives.
* :func:`plausibility` -- the share of samples above human limits (speed, acceleration).
* :func:`metabolic_power` -- the equivalent-slope model: accelerated running on flat ground costs as much as
  running uphill at constant speed on the slope ``ES = a / g`` with the body weight scaled by
  ``EM = sqrt(ES^2 + 1)`` (di Prampero, P. E. et al. (2005) Sprint running: a new energetic approach, J. Exp.
  Biol. 208, 2809-2816; Osgnach, C. et al. (2010) Energy cost and metabolic power in elite soccer: a new match
  analysis approach, Med. Sci. Sports Exerc. 42, 170-178, doi:10.1249/MSS.0b013e3181ae5cfd). The cost of running
  on a slope ``i`` is the polynomial of Minetti, A. E. et al. (2002) Energy cost of walking and running at extreme
  uphill and downhill slopes, J. Appl. Physiol. 93, 1039-1046:
  ``C(i) = 155.4 i^5 - 30.4 i^4 - 43.3 i^3 + 46.3 i^2 + 19.5 i + 3.6`` J/(kg m), valid for ``|i| <= 0.45``.
  Osgnach et al. multiply the cost by a terrain factor for grass; it is the ``terrain`` argument here (default 1:
  treadmill-equivalent values; take the factor from the paper before comparing with published match loads).
* :func:`predict_constant_velocity`, :func:`predict_limited`, :class:`MLPredictor` -- trajectory prediction
  baselines; :func:`reachable_radius` bounds any prediction by the player's acceleration and speed limits.

classes.name: MLPredictor
classes.doc:
Data-only displacement predictor: gradient-boosted trees (scikit-learn) on :func:`history_features`.

``residual_of="cv"`` learns the correction to the constant-velocity prediction instead of the raw displacement
(a physics prior the trees only correct); ``project=True`` projects the output onto the reachable set.

functions.name: kalman_smooth
functions.sig: (xy: np.ndarray, dt: float, *, sigma_pos: float = 0.1, jerk: float = 30.0, causal: bool = False, max_gap: float = 1.0) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]
functions.doc:
RTS-smoothed position, velocity and acceleration of tracks ``xy`` of shape ``(T, ..., 2)``.

The state per coordinate is ``(p, v, a)`` with white jerk of spectral density ``jerk**2`` (m^2/s^5) and
measurement noise ``sigma_pos`` (m). Returns ``pos, vel, acc`` (same shape as ``xy``) and ``pos_std, vel_std,
acc_std`` and the innovation log-likelihood ``loglik`` (for :func:`fit_noise`). NaN measurements are skipped (prediction only). The smoother is linear and exact for this model, so
its standard deviations are the posterior uncertainty given the stated noise levels. ``causal=True`` returns
the forward filter only (each estimate uses past samples only, as a real-time or a fair predictive use needs).

functions.name: fit_noise
functions.doc:
Measurement noise and jerk density by maximum marginal likelihood of :func:`kalman_smooth` (grid search on
the innovations): the data, not a guess, set how much the smoother trusts the samples.

functions.name: finite_differences
functions.sig: (xy: np.ndarray, dt: float) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]
functions.doc: Central differences of raw positions: ``vel``, ``acc`` (the data-only baseline with no smoothing).

functions.name: savgol_derivatives
functions.sig: (xy: np.ndarray, dt: float, window: float = 0.5, order: int = 2) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]
functions.doc: Savitzky-Golay smoothed position, velocity and acceleration (``window`` in seconds; NaN filled linearly).

functions.name: plausibility
functions.sig: (vel: np.ndarray, acc: np.ndarray, *, v_max: float = V_MAX, a_max: float = A_MAX) -> dict[str, float]
functions.doc: Share of finite samples whose speed exceeds ``v_max`` or whose acceleration magnitude exceeds ``a_max``.

functions.name: minetti_cost
functions.doc: Energy cost of running on slope ``i`` (Minetti et al. 2002), J/(kg m); ``i`` clipped to [-0.45, 0.45].

functions.name: metabolic_power
functions.sig: (speed, accel_fwd, *, terrain: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray
functions.doc:
Metabolic power in W/kg from speed (m/s) and forward acceleration (m/s^2), equivalent-slope model.

``ES = a / g``, ``EM = sqrt(ES^2 + 1)``, ``C = minetti_cost(ES) * EM * terrain``, ``P = C v``.

functions.name: forward_acceleration
functions.sig: (vel: np.ndarray, acc: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray
functions.doc: Component of the acceleration along the velocity (tangential), the input of :func:`metabolic_power`.

functions.name: reachable_radius
functions.sig: (speed0, horizon: float, *, v_max: float = V_MAX, a_max: float = A_MAX)
functions.doc:
Largest distance a player moving at ``speed0`` can cover in ``horizon`` s (accelerate at ``a_max`` up to
``v_max``): the physical bound on any displacement prediction.

functions.name: predict_constant_velocity
functions.sig: (pos, vel, horizon: float)
functions.doc: Position after ``horizon`` s at constant velocity.

functions.name: predict_limited
functions.sig: (pos, vel, acc, horizon: float, *, v_max: float = V_MAX, a_max: float = A_MAX, tau: float = 0.5, dt: float = 0.04)
functions.doc:
Physics prediction: the current acceleration (capped at ``a_max``) decays with time constant ``tau`` and the
speed is capped at ``v_max`` (players cannot keep accelerating; a simple first-order motor model).

functions.name: project_reachable
functions.sig: (pos, vel, pred, horizon: float, *, v_max: float = V_MAX, a_max: float = A_MAX)
functions.doc:
Project predictions onto the reachable set: the disc around the coasting point ``pos + vel * horizon`` of
radius ``a_max horizon^2 / 2`` intersected with the disc of radius :func:`reachable_radius` around ``pos``.

functions.name: history_features
functions.sig: (pos_hist: np.ndarray, ball_rel: np.ndarray | None = None) -> np.ndarray
functions.doc:
Features for the ML predictor: past positions relative to the current one (``(n, k, 2)`` -> ``(n, 2k)``),
optionally the ball position relative to the player.

functions.name: displacement_errors
functions.sig: (pred, true, pos = None, vel = None, horizon: float | None = None) -> dict[str, float]
functions.doc:
Mean and 90th-percentile final displacement error (m); with ``pos, vel, horizon`` also the share of
predictions outside the physically reachable set.

children.name: pinneapple_systems.sports.football.metrics
children.doc:
Scores for probabilistic binary predictions: log-loss, Brier, ROC AUC, calibration (reliability bins, ECE) and
bootstrap intervals of score differences between two models on the same events.

functions.doc: Mean predicted probability, observed frequency and count per bin (``quantile`` or ``uniform`` bins).

functions.name: ece
functions.sig: (p, y, bins: int = 10) -> float
functions.doc: Expected calibration error with quantile bins.

functions.name: score
functions.sig: (p, y) -> dict[str, float]
functions.doc: All scores of one model.

functions.name: paired_bootstrap

Difference ``metric(a) - metric(b)`` on the same events with a 95 % bootstrap interval (negative: a better

children.name: pinneapple_systems.sports.football.pc_study

functions.name: physics_features
functions.sig: (ps: PC.PassSet, p: PC.PCParams) -> np.ndarray
functions.doc: Pitch-control probability, earliest attacker and defender intercept times minus the ball travel time.

functions.name: fit_models
functions.sig: (train: PC.PassSet, *, seed: int = 0, which = ('pc_default', 'pc_reaction', 'pc_accel', 'logistic', 'gbm', 'hybrid')) -> dict[str, Any]

children.name: pinneapple_systems.sports.football.pitch_control
children.doc:
Pitch control: who wins the ball at a target point, from player kinematics and ball travel time.

The model of Spearman, W. (2018) Beyond Expected Goals, MIT Sloan Sports Analytics Conference: every player ``j``
reaches the target at an uncertain time with logistic CDF ``P_j(T) = 1 / (1 + exp(-pi / (sqrt(3) sigma)
(T - tau_j)))`` around his time to intercept ``tau_j``; once there he controls the ball at rate ``lambda_j``; the
control probabilities of the two teams follow ::

    dPPCF_j/dT = (1 - PPCF_att(T) - PPCF_def(T)) P_j(T) lambda_j,     T >= ball arrival time

integrated here with explicit Euler steps of ``dt`` (reimplemented from the paper's equations).

Time-to-intercept models (:func:`time_to_intercept`):

* ``"reaction"`` -- the player keeps his velocity for a reaction time, then runs straight at ``v_max`` (the
  simple form most open implementations use);
* ``"accel"`` -- acceleration-limited motion from the current velocity: the reachable set after ``t`` is the
  disc around the coasting point with the radius covered from rest at ``a_max`` up to ``v_max``; ``tau`` is the
  first ``t`` whose disc holds the target (bisection).

Ball travel time: constant speed (``ball_speed``) or the rolling-ball model of :mod:`.ball` with a kick speed that
grows with the pass length (fitted to the passes of the training match by :func:`fit_ball_travel`).

:func:`fit_params` fits the free parameters by maximum likelihood of observed pass outcomes, so the comparison
with a data-only classifier is at equal data.

children.doc:
Expected goals with and without physics: a standard shot-geometry baseline against intercept-time features
computed from the StatsBomb 360 freeze frame.

Standard features (what most public xG models use): distance and angle to goal, header, body part, first time,
under pressure, free kick, play pattern.

Physics features (:func:`physics_features`, 2-D, ball height ignored): the ball travels in a straight line from
the shot to each of ``n_mouth`` points of the goal mouth at speed ``v_shot``; a player at distance ``d`` from a
point of that path can intercept it if ``reaction + max(d - reach, 0) / v_player <= t_ball``, with a larger
``reach`` and a lower ``reaction`` for the goalkeeper (dive). From that:

* ``open_fraction`` -- share of the goal mouth no opponent can intercept (the physics analogue of the visible
  goal angle);
* ``gk_margin`` -- the keeper's best time margin over the mouth (negative: he cannot get there in time);
* ``blockers`` -- outfield opponents able to intercept the path to the goal centre.

Units: StatsBomb coordinates are yards (120 x 80, goal posts at y = 36 and 44 on x = 120); converted to metres.
:func:`select_params` chooses ``v_shot`` and the keeper's speed from a small grid on the training shots only.

children.name: pinneapple_systems.time_series.adaptive
children.doc:
Adaptive forecasting: switch between and combine forecasting models online, using only past out-of-sample errors.

Every expert (any object with ``fit(y) -> self`` and ``predict(horizon) -> array``: the built-in fast models below,
the baselines and ML forecasters of ``pinneapple_systems.time_series``, or your own) is refitted on the data seen so
far and issues forecasts for horizons 1..H. When the observation for a forecast arrives, its error updates the
weights. Nothing ever looks at data the forecast could not have known: the procedure is prequential (Dawid 1984),
which is what prevents overfitting the model choice to the evaluation period.

Three levels:

1. **Fixed-Share exponential weights per horizon** (Herbster & Warmuth 1998, Machine Learning 32:151). Weights
   shrink by exp(-eta * loss) and a share alpha is redistributed every step, so the mixture can move to a different
   model when the regime changes (a plain exponential-weights / "best model so far" rule takes far too long to switch).
   Regret is bounded against the best *sequence* of models with a limited number of switches.
2. **A grid of (eta, alpha) aggregators combined by AdaHedge** (de Rooij, van Erven, Grunwald & Koolen 2014, JMLR
   15:1281), which needs no tuning: the learning rate and the switching rate are themselves chosen online, with a
   regret bound against the best (eta, alpha) in hindsight.
3. **Adaptive conformal intervals** (Gibbs & Candes 2021, NeurIPS): the interval level is corrected online after every
   miss or hit, so coverage stays near the target even when the distribution shifts.

Losses are scale-free: absolute (or squared) error divided by the mean absolute one-step change of the series so far
(the MASE scale), clipped to keep them bounded as the theory assumes.

classes.name: HoltDamped
classes.doc: Holt's linear trend with damping phi (Gardner & McKenzie 1985).

classes.name: Theta
classes.doc:
Theta method as SES with drift equal to half the regression slope (Assimakopoulos & Nikolopoulos 2000;
Hyndman & Billah 2003, Int. J. Forecasting 19:287).

classes.name: RidgeAR
classes.doc:
Autoregression of order p with an intercept, ridge-regularised, fitted on the last ``window`` points; multi-step
forecasts are recursive.

classes.name: LagRegressorExpert
classes.sig: (estimator: Any, n_lags: int = 12, refit_every: int = 24, window: int = 500)
classes.doc:
Any tabular regressor (scikit-learn style ``fit(X, y)`` / ``predict(X)``, including the ML forecasters of
``pinneapple_systems.time_series.models``) as an expert: lagged values as features, recursive multi-step forecasts.
The estimator is refitted every ``refit_every`` calls (on the last ``window`` points); in between only the lag
tail is updated, so an expensive model does not slow every step.

classes.name: AdaptiveRun
classes.doc: Result of :meth:`AdaptiveForecaster.run`: one row per forecast origin t (forecasts for t+1..t+H).

methods.name: errors
methods.doc:
MAE, RMSE and MASE at horizon ``h`` for the ensemble and every expert, on the origins whose target is
observed; plus the best single expert in hindsight (not available online: an upper bar, not a competitor
the ensemble could have known).

methods.name: switches
methods.doc: (origin, expert) each time the leading expert changes.

classes.name: AdaptiveForecaster
classes.sig: (experts: Mapping[str, Any] | Sequence[Any], horizon: int = 1, mode: str = 'combine', etas: Sequence[float] = (0.5, 2.0, 8.0), alphas: Sequence[float] = (0.0, 0.01, 0.05), loss: str = 'absolute', clip: float = 10.0, interval_level: float | None = 0.9, conformal_gamma: float = 0.01, refit_every: int = 1, max_history: int | None = 1000, on_error: str = 'fallback')
classes.doc:
Online selection and combination of forecasting models.

>>> af = AdaptiveForecaster(default_experts(season_length=12), horizon=6)
>>> run = af.run(y, start=48)          # backtest: every origin uses only data up to that origin
>>> run.errors(h=1)["ensemble"], run.switches()
>>> af.forecast()                      # next H values, interval and current weights

``mode``: "combine" (weighted average, default) or "select" (the forecast of the leading expert, i.e. switching
between models). ``etas`` / ``alphas``: the (learning rate, switching rate) grid of the Fixed-Share aggregators,
combined by AdaHedge. ``refit_every``: refit experts every k steps (expensive experts); forecasts are reissued from
the last fit in between.

methods.doc: Feed one new observation: score the forecasts that targeted it, then refit and issue new forecasts.

methods.name: forecast
methods.doc: Forecast for the next H steps from everything fed so far, with interval and weights.

methods.doc: Backtest: feed ``y`` one value at a time; record the forecasts issued at every origin >= ``start``.

children.name: pinneapple_systems.time_series.classical_wrappers
children.doc:
Real wrappers around the classical statistical forecasting libraries.

`statsmodels` and `pmdarima` are listed in this package's `timeseries` extra
(`pyproject.toml`) but, prior to this module, were only genuinely wired into
statistical *tests* (ADF/KPSS/ACF/PACF in `audit/tests.py`,
`eda/plots.py`) and STL decomposition (`pinneapple_simulation`) — never into
an actual forecasting model. `pinneapple_neural.architectures.classical_ts.ARIMA`
looks like an ARIMA model but is a hand-rolled ridge-regression AR(p) on
Δ^d(x); it does not call `statsmodels` and has no MA component. `pmdarima`
had zero references anywhere in the repo.

This module closes that gap with two forecasters that follow the same
`.fit(y) -> self` / `.predict(horizon) -> np.ndarray` convention used by
`pinneapple_systems.time_series.baselines.naive.NaiveForecaster` and friends:

- `StatsmodelsARIMAForecaster` — real wrapper around
  `statsmodels.tsa.statespace.sarimax.SARIMAX` (a strict superset of
  `statsmodels.tsa.arima.model.ARIMA` that additionally supports seasonal
  orders), giving genuine ARIMA/SARIMA fitting (including the MA terms the
  hand-rolled `classical_ts.ARIMA` omits).
- `AutoARIMAForecaster` — real wrapper around `pmdarima.auto_arima`, which
  automatically selects (p,d,q)(P,D,Q,m) via stepwise search — a genuine
  capability neither the hand-rolled ARIMA nor the plain statsmodels wrapper
  above provides.

Both treat their backing library as optional (try/except ImportError with an
actionable `pip install ...` message), following the pattern already used by
`models/classical.py` (`XGBoostForecaster`, `CatBoostForecaster`, ...).

classes.name: StatsmodelsARIMAForecaster
classes.doc:
Real ARIMA/SARIMA forecaster wrapping `statsmodels`.

Uses `statsmodels.tsa.statespace.sarimax.SARIMAX`, which fits the same
ARIMA(p,d,q) family as `statsmodels.tsa.arima.model.ARIMA` but also
supports an optional seasonal order (P,D,Q,m) — set
`seasonal_order=(0, 0, 0, 0)` (the default) to fall back to plain
non-seasonal ARIMA.

Example:
    >>> f = StatsmodelsARIMAForecaster(order=(2, 1, 1))
    >>> f.fit(y)
    >>> y_hat = f.predict(horizon=10)

methods.name: predict_with_uncertainty
methods.doc: Returns (mean, std) using the model's analytic forecast variance.

classes.name: AutoARIMAForecaster
classes.doc:
Real forecaster wrapping `pmdarima.auto_arima`.

Automatically selects the (p,d,q) — and, if `seasonal=True`, seasonal
(P,D,Q,m) — order via stepwise AIC-minimizing search, then fits the
resulting SARIMAX model. This is a genuine differentiator from both the
hand-rolled `classical_ts.ARIMA` (fixed order, no search) and
`StatsmodelsARIMAForecaster` above (also a fixed, user-specified order).

Example:
    >>> f = AutoARIMAForecaster(seasonal=False)
    >>> f.fit(y)
    >>> y_hat = f.predict(horizon=10)
    >>> f.order_   # the (p, d, q) auto_arima selected

methods.name: predict_with_uncertainty
methods.doc: Returns (mean, std) derived from pmdarima's confidence intervals.

children.summary: Real wrappers around the classical statistical forecasting libraries.

children.name: pinneapple_systems.time_series.csv_loader
children.doc:
CSV → tensor loader for time series datasets.

Supports:
  - Any CSV with 1 to N numerical columns (univariate or multivariate)
  - Optional datetime column for sorting
  - Missing-value imputation (forward-fill, back-fill, or linear interpolation)
  - Channel-wise z-score normalisation fitted on the train split only
    (no leakage into val/test)
  - Automatic train/val/test temporal splits

Typical usage::

    from pinneapple_systems.time_series.csv_loader import load_timeseries_csv

    result = load_timeseries_csv(
        "data/temperature.csv",
        target_cols=["T_indoor", "T_outdoor"],
        time_col="timestamp",
        normalize=True,
        train_ratio=0.70,
        val_ratio=0.15,
    )

    train_tensor = result["train_tensor"]   # (T_train, F) float32
    val_tensor   = result["val_tensor"]     # (T_val,   F)
    test_tensor  = result["test_tensor"]    # (T_test,  F)
    scaler       = result["scaler"]         # TimeSeriesScaler for inverse-transform
    meta         = result["meta"]           # dict with shapes, column names, etc.

classes.sig: () -> None
classes.doc:
Channel-wise z-score scaler: fit on training data, apply to all splits.

Avoids data leakage by only computing mean/std from the training portion.
Stores running mean and std so any slice can be (inverse-)transformed later.

methods.doc: Compute channel statistics from training data.  y: (T, F) or (T,).

methods.doc: Standardise y using fitted statistics.  y: (T, F) or (T,).

functions.name: load_timeseries_csv
functions.sig: (path: Union[str, Path], *, target_cols: Optional[List[str]] = None, feature_cols: Optional[List[str]] = None, time_col: Optional[str] = None, fill_method: str = 'ffill', normalize: bool = True, train_ratio: float = 0.7, val_ratio: float = 0.15) -> Dict
functions.doc:
Load a CSV file and return train / val / test tensors ready for PINNeAPPle.

The split is strictly temporal (no shuffling) to prevent look-ahead leakage.
Normalisation statistics are fitted on the training split only.

Args:
    path:        Path to the CSV file.
    target_cols: Columns to include as model targets.  If None, all numeric
                 columns (excluding time_col) are used.
    feature_cols: Additional exogenous feature columns to append.  If None,
                  no extra features are added beyond target_cols.
    time_col:    Optional column name containing timestamps.  When provided
                 the DataFrame is sorted chronologically before splitting.
    fill_method: Strategy for missing values: ``"ffill"`` (forward-fill),
                 ``"bfill"`` (back-fill), or ``"linear"`` (interpolation).
    normalize:   If True, apply channel-wise z-score normalisation fitted
                 on the training split.
    train_ratio: Fraction of time steps for training (default 0.70).
    val_ratio:   Fraction of time steps for validation (default 0.15).
                 The remainder  ``1 - train_ratio - val_ratio``  becomes the
                 test set.

Returns:
    A dict with the following keys:

    ``series_tensor``  (T, F) float32 — full normalised series.
    ``train_tensor``   (T_train, F) float32
    ``val_tensor``     (T_val,   F) float32
    ``test_tensor``    (T_test,  F) float32
    ``scaler``         :class:`TimeSeriesScaler` or ``None`` when normalize=False.
    ``meta``           dict — shape info, column names, split sizes.
    ``raw_df``         pandas DataFrame before normalisation (original values).

functions.name: generate_synthetic_csv
functions.sig: (path: Union[str, Path], T: int = 1000, seed: int = 42, freq: str = 'D') -> Path
functions.doc:
Generate a synthetic multivariate time series CSV and save it to *path*.

Creates three channels:
  - ``y1``: linear trend + two seasonal components + noise (main target)
  - ``y2``: different seasonality + weak cross-correlation with y1
  - ``y3``: weak trend + single seasonal component + higher noise

Args:

    seed:  Random seed for reproducibility.
    freq:  Pandas frequency string used to build the datetime index.

children.name: pinneapple_systems.time_series.decomposition.fft_lstm
children.doc:
Hybrid FFT decomposition + LSTM residual forecaster (multivariate-ready).

Architecture:
  1. FFTDecomposer  — per-channel FFT that extracts trend + dominant harmonics
                      and exposes deterministic reconstruction / extrapolation.
  2. ResidualLSTMForecaster — PyTorch LSTM that models only the *residual* after
                              FFT reconstruction. Plugs directly into the standard
                              Trainer + TSDataModule pipeline.
  3. FFTLSTMPipeline — high-level orchestrator that wires the two stages and
                       exposes fit_fft / residuals_tensor / fft_extrapolation helpers.

Multivariate support:
  Each channel receives its own FFTForecaster instance; the LSTM processes the
  joint residual tensor (B, L, F) and predicts (B, H, n_targets).

Anti-overfitting in ResidualLSTMForecaster:
  - Input LayerNorm (normalises across feature dimension, batch-size agnostic)
  - LSTM inter-layer dropout
  - LayerNorm on the final LSTM hidden state
  - Dropout before the linear head
  - Weight-decay (L2) is handled at the optimizer level via TrainConfig.weight_decay
  - Gradient clipping via TrainConfig.grad_clip
  - EarlyStopping via the standard callback from pinneapple_train.callbacks

Args:

    detrend:         remove linear trend before FFT.

                     threshold instead of a fixed count.
    auto_threshold:  fraction of max amplitude for automatic selection.

classes.sig: (cfg: Optional[ResidualLSTMConfig] = None, **kw)
classes.doc:
LSTM forecaster trained on FFT residuals.

Input:  (B, L, n_features)  — windowed residual series
Output: TSOutput(y_hat=(B, H, n_targets), extras={})

Anti-overfitting checklist (use together with optimizer weight_decay and
EarlyStopping from pinneapple_train.callbacks):
  ✓ Input LayerNorm  (safe for any batch size, unlike BatchNorm)
  ✓ LSTM inter-layer dropout
  ✓ LayerNorm on LSTM last-step hidden state
  ✓ Dropout before linear head
  (set weight_decay in TrainConfig, grad_clip ≥ 0.5 recommended)

classes.name: FFTLSTMPipeline
classes.sig: (*, n_harmonics: int = 10, detrend: bool = True, auto_harmonics: bool = True, auto_threshold: float = 0.05, input_len: int = 64, horizon: int = 16, n_features: int = 1, n_targets: int = 1, hidden_size: int = 128, num_layers: int = 2, dropout: float = 0.2) -> None
classes.doc:
Orchestrates the two-stage hybrid FFT + LSTM pipeline.

Stage 1 (FFT): fits a multivariate FFTDecomposer on the *training* portion
  of the series, capturing global trend and dominant periodic components.

Stage 2 (LSTM): trains a ResidualLSTMForecaster on the stochastic residual
  (original − FFT reconstruction) using the standard Trainer infrastructure.

Final forecast = FFT extrapolation  +  LSTM residual prediction

Typical usage::

    pipeline = FFTLSTMPipeline(
        n_harmonics=12, input_len=96, horizon=24, n_features=3, n_targets=3
    )

    # Step 1 — fit FFT on training data (numpy)
    pipeline.fit_fft(train_np)                   # (T_train, F)

    # Step 2 — compute residual series (for ALL splits)
    res_tensor = pipeline.residuals_tensor(full_series_np)  # (T, F)

    # Step 3 — build TSDataModule on residuals, train with Trainer
    dm  = TSDataModule(series=res_tensor, spec=spec, ...)
    mdl = pipeline.build_lstm()
    trainer.fit(train_loader, val_loader, cfg)   # standard Trainer call

    # Step 4 — inference: reconstruct final forecast
    fft_part  = pipeline.fft_extrapolation(start=T_train, horizon=24)
    lstm_part = mdl(x_residual_window).y_hat.numpy()
    forecast  = fft_part + lstm_part

children.name: pinneapple_systems.time_series.decomposition.hht_lstm
children.doc:
Hilbert-Huang Transform (EMD-based) + LSTM residual forecaster (multivariate-ready).

Architecture:
  1. HHTDecomposer  — per-channel Empirical Mode Decomposition that extracts dominant
                      IMFs (Intrinsic Mode Functions) and the linear trend; extrapolates
                      them forward via Hilbert instantaneous frequency/amplitude.
  2. HHTLSTMPipeline — high-level orchestrator mirroring FFTLSTMPipeline; exposes
                       fit_hht / residuals_tensor / hht_extrapolation helpers.
  3. The residual LSTM (ResidualLSTMForecaster from fft_lstm.py) is reused directly.

Key difference from FFT approach:
  • FFT assumes stationarity with a fixed frequency basis.
  • EMD is fully data-adaptive — IMFs are extracted from the signal itself, capturing
    non-stationary amplitude and frequency modulation.
  • Better for signals with evolving seasonality; less reliable for very long extrapolation.

Dependencies: PyEMD (pip install EMD-signal), scipy.

    detrend:               remove linear trend before EMD.

Orchestrates HHTDecomposer + LSTM residual forecasting.

Mirrors FFTLSTMPipeline API so both pipelines can be used interchangeably.

Usage::

    pipeline.fit_hht(train_np)                          # fit on train only

children.name: pinneapple_systems.time_series.enso
pinneapple_systems.time_series.enso.data
children.doc:
Openly licensed ENSO observations, downloaded once, reduced to monthly tropical-Pacific products and cached with
the SHA-256 of every source file.

Sources (all without credentials; NOAA data are public domain, ERA5 is under the Copernicus licence):

* **SST** -- NOAA OISST v2.1 (AVHRR-only, daily, 0.25 deg; Huang et al. 2021, J. Climate 34:2923; Reynolds et al.
  2007, J. Climate 20:5473) from the NOAA Open Data Dissemination bucket on AWS
  (``noaa-cdr-sea-surface-temp-optimum-interpolation-pds``). :func:`oisst_monthly` averages every final (not
  preliminary) daily file of a month into 1 deg cells over the tropical Pacific. The Nino indices are cos-latitude
  weighted box means of that field (:data:`NINO_BOXES`).
* **Thermocline** -- 20 deg C isotherm depth (D20) from the moored-buoy (TAO/TRITON) and, optionally, XBT profiles
  of the World Ocean Database (Boyer et al. 2018, NOAA Atlas NESDIS 87; AWS bucket ``noaa-wod-pds``).
  :func:`wod_d20_casts` interpolates D20 in every quality-controlled cast; :func:`d20_monthly` bins them into
  monthly longitude bins. The warm-water-volume proxy is the zonal mean D20 anomaly over 5S-5N, 120E-80W (the
  region of Meinen & McPhaden 2000, J. Climate 13:3551).
* **Atmosphere** -- ERA5 (Hersbach et al. 2020, QJRMS 146:1999) 6-hourly 10 m wind, mean sea-level pressure and SST
  on the 64 x 32 (5.625 deg) grid of WeatherBench 2 (Rasp et al. 2024, JAMES 16:e2023MS004019; bucket
  ``gs://weatherbench2``), 1959-01 to 2023-01: :func:`era5_monthly`. Zonal wind stress from the bulk formula, and a
  Tahiti-minus-Darwin pressure index (:func:`soi_from_mslp`) at the nearest grid cells.
* **Cross-checks** -- NCEI 0-700 m ocean heat content, 3-month means 1955-2020 (Levitus et al. 2012, GRL
  39:L10603; bucket ``noaa-cdr-ocean-heat-content-pds``): :func:`ncei_heat_content`. The statsmodels El Nino data
  set (Nino 1+2 SST 1950-2010, NOAA CPC): :func:`statsmodels_nino12`.

Every downloaded file is hashed and recorded in a manifest (``<cache>/enso/manifest_<product>.json``: URL ->
SHA-256 and size). Passing ``manifest=`` (a manifest written by an earlier run, e.g. the one committed with the
study) makes a download that does not reproduce a recorded hash raise instead of returning different data. Large
raw files are deleted once reduced; their hashes stay in the manifest.

Depth [m] where the profile first crosses ``iso`` going down (linear interpolation between the bracketing

children.name: pinneapple_systems.time_series.enso.evaluation
children.doc:
ENSO-specific scores on top of the forecast_lab ones: anomaly correlation per lead, skill stratified by target
calendar month (the spring predictability barrier), categorical El Nino / neutral / La Nina verification, and a
blocked cross-validated hindcast that gives every year an out-of-sample forecast for cheap models.

functions.sig: (mean: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray) -> list[float]
functions.doc:
Anomaly correlation (Pearson, over origins) per horizon column.

Returns
-------
acc : list[float] [-]
    Anomaly correlation per horizon.

functions.name: by_target_month
functions.sig: (mean: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, origins: np.ndarray, month_of_year: np.ndarray, horizons: Sequence[int], min_n: int = 6) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc: ACC and RMSE for each (target calendar month, horizon); NaN where fewer than ``min_n`` forecasts.

functions.sig: (x: np.ndarray, threshold: float = 0.5) -> np.ndarray
functions.doc:
-1 La Nina (x <= -threshold), 0 neutral, +1 El Nino (x >= threshold).

Returns
-------
category : np.ndarray [-]
    -1, 0 or +1.

functions.name: categorical
functions.sig: (mean: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, threshold: float = 0.5) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
Per horizon: 3 x 3 contingency table (rows observed La Nina / neutral / El Nino, columns forecast), hit rate
(probability of detection) of each category, false-alarm ratio of the warm and cold categories, accuracy, and
the Heidke skill score (accuracy relative to random forecasts with the same marginals).

functions.name: blocked_hindcast
functions.sig: (make: Callable[[], Forecaster], data: SeriesData, horizons: Sequence[int], *, block: int = 48, first: int = 36, last: int | None = None, val_frac: float = 0.15) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
Out-of-sample forecasts for every origin in [first, last]: the origins are cut into blocks of ``block``
months; each block is forecast by a model fitted on all other origins whose targets end more than max(h)
before the block or start after it (purged on both sides), with its last ``val_frac`` (in time) as the
validation block. Returns origins, mean, std and targets (n, nh). Data after ``last + max(h)`` are never used.
Meant for cheap models (one fit per block) and for the stratified skill, not as a substitute for the
untouched test period.

children.name: pinneapple_systems.time_series.enso.forecasters
children.doc:
ENSO forecasters with the :class:`~pinneapple_systems.time_series.forecast_lab.Forecaster` interface, so the
forecast_lab protocol (purged walk-forward tuning, untouched test period, DM tests) applies to them unchanged.

They read the monthly indices from ``data.obs`` (columns named in ``data.meta["columns"]``, see
:func:`.dataset.to_series`) and the maps from ``data.meta`` (``sst_maps``, ``d20_band``, ``taux``, ...); a
forecast from origin t uses rows <= t only, and everything estimated (EOFs, coefficients, couplings) comes from rows
before ``train_end`` of the training origins.

* :class:`ColumnSubset` -- run any forecaster on a subset of the columns (e.g. the forecast_lab ODE, UDE, SINDy
  and EnKF forecasters on the (T, h) pair).
* :class:`RechargeOscillatorForecaster` -- :mod:`.oscillators` recharge oscillator, deterministic or stochastic
  (ensemble), optionally seasonal and with multiplicative noise.
* :class:`LIMForecaster` -- linear inverse model (Penland & Sardeshmukh 1995, J. Climate 8:1999) on the leading
  SST EOFs plus thermocline indices, with its analytic Gaussian forecast distribution.
* :class:`MapCNNForecaster` -- convolutional network on the last months of SST anomaly maps plus thermocline
  indices (the design of Ham et al. 2019, Nature 573:568, scaled down), optionally pre-trained on a long stochastic
  run of the intermediate model fitted to the training period.
* :class:`IntermediateModelForecaster` -- the coupled model of :mod:`.intermediate`, fitted to the training
  period (:func:`fit_intermediate`) and initialised either by SST nudging or by a localised ensemble Kalman filter
  that assimilates SST maps and D20 bins (``init="enkf"``).
* :class:`EnsembleForecaster` -- equal-weight multi-model ensemble (mixture of the members' distributions).

classes.name: ColumnSubset
classes.sig: (inner: Forecaster, cols: Sequence[str], name: str | None = None, family: str | None = None)
classes.doc: Wrap ``inner`` so that it sees only ``cols`` (names in ``data.meta["columns"]``; the target must be one).

classes.name: RechargeOscillatorForecaster
classes.sig: (h_col: str = 'wwv', seasonal: Sequence[str] = (), multiplicative: bool = False, stochastic: bool = True, n_members: int = 200, sub: int = 4, seed: int = 0, name: str | None = None, family: str | None = None)
classes.doc:
Jin's recharge oscillator on (T, h) = (``target`` column, ``h_col``), fitted on the training segment.

``stochastic``: ensemble of ``n_members`` Euler-Maruyama paths (its own predictive distribution); otherwise the
deterministic RK4 path with a Gaussian spread calibrated on the validation block.

classes.name: LIMForecaster
classes.sig: (n_eofs: int = 10, extra_cols: Sequence[str] = ('wwv',), tau0: int = 1, name: str | None = None)
classes.doc:
Linear inverse model dx/dt = L x + noise on x = (leading ``n_eofs`` PCs of the SST anomaly maps, the
``extra_cols`` indices), each standardised; L = log(C(tau0) C(0)^-1) / tau0 from the training segment; the
target is read out by least squares on x. Forecast mean a . exp(L h) x(t), variance
a . (C(0) - G(h) C(0) G(h)^T) . a + readout residual variance (Gaussian; Penland & Sardeshmukh 1995).

classes.name: MapCNNForecaster
classes.sig: (n_lags: int = 3, pool: int = 2, scalar_cols: Sequence[str] = ('wwv', 'h_west', 'h_east'), channels: tuple[int, int] = (16, 32), hidden: int = 64, dropout: float = 0.1, weight_decay: float = 0.001, lr: float = 0.001, epochs: int = 150, patience: int = 15, batch_size: int = 32, n_members: int = 5, pretrain: dict | None = None, seed: int = 0, name: str | None = None, family: str | None = None)
classes.doc:
CNN on the last ``n_lags`` monthly SST anomaly maps (coarsened by ``pool``) plus scalars (``scalar_cols`` at
the origin and the sine / cosine of the origin month); outputs the standardised change of the target at every
horizon (persistence = zero output). ``n_members`` seeds are averaged.

``pretrain`` (dict, e.g. ``{"years": 400, "members": 8}``): first fit :class:`IntermediateModelForecaster`'s
coupled model on the same training segment, run it with stochastic winds for that many model years, train on
the synthetic maps and indices, then fine-tune on the observations (Ham et al. 2019 pre-trained on CMIP5 runs;
here the long run comes from a physical model fitted to the training years only, so no test year leaks in).

classes.name: IntermediateModelForecaster
classes.sig: (init: str = 'nudged', n_members: int = 1, enkf_members: int = 24, coupling: float = 1.0, eps_a: float = 0.1, c: float = 2.7, r_days: float = 900.0, nudge_days: float = 5.0, sst_err: float = 0.3, d20_err: float = 8.0, inflation: float = 1.05, loc_lon: float = 25.0, loc_lat: float = 8.0, seed: int = 0, name: str | None = None, family: str | None = None)
classes.doc:
The coupled intermediate model fitted on the training segment (:func:`fit_intermediate`).

``init="nudged"``: one continuous run with the SST nudged to the observed maps (5-day time scale) and the ocean
driven by the model's own winds gives the state at every origin (only data up to the origin); forecasts are
deterministic (``n_members=1``) or stochastic-wind ensembles. ``init="enkf"``: a localised stochastic EnKF of
``enkf_members`` members assimilates the monthly SST anomaly maps (|lat| <= 10, every second cell, error
``sst_err``) and the observed 5S-5N D20 bins (error ``d20_err``) month by month; forecasts start from the
analysis members (``n_members`` of them) with stochastic winds.

methods.name: forecast_fields
methods.sig: (data, origins, n_months: int | None = None, chunk: int = 400)
methods.doc: Monthly mean T and h maps of the forecasts from ``origins``: arrays (months, [members,] origins, ny, nx).

classes.name: EnsembleForecaster
classes.sig: (members: Sequence[Forecaster], n_draw: int = 100, seed: int = 0, name: str | None = None, family: str | None = None)
classes.doc:
Equal-weight mixture of fitted-together members: mean = mean of the members' means; samples = ``n_draw``
draws from each member's distribution (its samples, or its Gaussian).

functions.name: box_index
functions.sig: (maps: np.ndarray, grid: IM.OceanGrid, box = (-5.0, 5.0, 190.0, 240.0)) -> np.ndarray
functions.doc: cos-latitude weighted box mean of maps (..., ny, nx) on ``grid`` (default the Nino 3.4 box).

functions.name: ro_rhs
functions.doc: Constant-coefficient recharge oscillator vector field on (T, h) for the forecast_lab ODE forecasters.

functions.name: fit_intermediate
functions.sig: (meta: dict[str, Any], end: int, *, eps_a: float = 0.1, c: float = 2.7, r_days: float = 900.0, coupling: float = 1.0, window: int = 4, ridge: float = 0.001, L_T: float = 6.0, dt_hours: float = 8.0, atm_every: int = 15, hindcast: bool = True, log = None) -> tuple[IM.CoupledModel, dict[str, Any]]
functions.doc:
Fit the coupled model to the rows [0, end) of the study data (``meta`` of :func:`.dataset.to_series`).

1. The atmosphere's coupling mu: least squares of the ERA5 zonal stress anomalies (130E-80W, 10S-10N) on the Gill
   winds of the observed SST anomalies. The stochastic forcing ``noise_tau`` is the standard deviation of the
   residual stress.
2. The ocean (c, r fixed) forced by the ERA5 stress over the same months: its equatorial h is regressed on the
   observed 2S-2N D20 anomalies to give the amplitude factor ``h_scale`` (model h -> D20), and its correlation
   with them is the ocean hindcast check.
3. The SST equation per longitude (pooled over +-``window`` cells): monthly change of the equatorial (2S-2N)
   SST anomaly regressed on T, the observed D20 anomaly (in model units) and the model's own coupled stress.
``coupling`` scales mu afterwards (a tuning knob for the coupled stability).

children.summary: ENSO forecasters with the ~pinneapple_systems.time_series.forecast_lab.Forecaster interface, so the forecast_lab protocol (purged walk-forward tuning, untouched test period, DM tests) applies to them ...

children.name: pinneapple_systems.time_series.enso.intermediate
children.doc:
An intermediate coupled model of the tropical Pacific in the spirit of Zebiak & Cane (1987, Mon. Wea. Rev.
115:2262), simplified, and the checks that every component is solved correctly.

* :class:`ShallowWaterOcean` -- linear reduced-gravity (first baroclinic mode) ocean on the equatorial beta-plane,
  Arakawa C-grid, closed basin 120E-80W (walls east and west, sponge layers north and south), Rayleigh friction
  and Newtonian damping r, wind-stress forcing tau / (rho H), RK4 in time. Free waves: the equatorial Kelvin wave
  at c = sqrt(g' H) and long Rossby waves at c / (2n + 1) (Matsuno 1966, J. Met. Soc. Japan 44:25), which reflect at
  the boundaries -- the delayed-oscillator memory of the ocean.
* :class:`GillAtmosphere` -- the steady damped long-wave response to a heating Q (Gill 1980, QJRMS 106:447) solved
  exactly per meridional mode: Q is projected on parabolic-cylinder (Hermite) functions; the Kelvin mode
  (eps + d/dx) q0 = -Q0 and the Rossby modes ((2n + 1) eps - d/dx) q_{n+1} = -(Q_{n-1} + 2n Q_{n+1}) / 2 are solved
  by FFT on a periodic longitude circle; u = (q - r) / 2, p = (q + r) / 2 with r_n = 2 (n + 2) q_{n+2}.
  :func:`gill_analytic` is the closed-form solution for Q = F(x) exp(-y^2 / 2) by periodic Green's functions.
* :func:`sst_tendency` -- the SST anomaly equation dT/dt = -eps_T T + gamma(x) S(y) h + kappa(x) S(y) tau_x (local
  damping, thermocline feedback, Ekman-upwelling / wind feedback), coefficients per longitude estimated from data.
* :class:`CoupledModel` -- ocean + SST + atmosphere (tau = mu * Gill(T), mu fitted to ERA5 stress), optional
  stochastic wind forcing and SST nudging; vectorised over a leading ensemble axis.

Validation (each returns measured vs theory): :func:`kelvin_wave_test`, :func:`rossby_wave_test`,
:func:`gill_test`, :func:`convergence_study`.

classes.name: OceanGrid
classes.doc: C-grid: h and T at cell centres (ny, nx); u on the nx + 1 west/east faces; v on the ny + 1 south/north faces.

classes.name: ShallowWaterOcean
classes.sig: (grid: OceanGrid | None = None, c: float = 2.7, H: float = 150.0, r_days: float = 900.0, sponge_deg: float = 5.0, sponge_days: float = 5.0, dtype: str = 'float64')
classes.doc:
Linear reduced-gravity shallow water on the equatorial beta-plane (dimensional, SI units).

du/dt =  f v - g' dh/dx + tau_x / (rho H) - r u
dv/dt = -f u - g' dh/dy + tau_y / (rho H) - r v
dh/dt = -H (du/dx + dv/dy) - r h,          f = beta y,   g' = c^2 / H

``r_days`` is the damping time; a sponge raises the damping to 1 / ``sponge_days`` over the ``sponge_deg``
nearest the north and south walls. States are dicts of arrays (NumPy or torch) with any leading batch shape;
the arithmetic runs in torch (``dtype``), which is several times faster than NumPy for ensembles.

methods.name: max_dt
methods.doc:
A safe RK4 step: 2.6 / sqrt(largest gravity-wave frequency^2 + largest f^2) (the RK4 stability limit
on the imaginary axis is 2.83).

methods.name: step
methods.doc: One RK4 step (stress held fixed). NumPy in, NumPy out; torch in, torch out.

classes.name: GillAtmosphere
classes.sig: (eps: float = 0.1, c_a: float = 60.0, n_modes: int = 24, dlon: float = 2.5, lon_offset: float = 0.0)
classes.doc:
Gill (1980) long-wave response in Matsuno units (y in L_a = sqrt(c_a / beta), x in L_a, Q per unit heating).

``solve(Q, lat, lon)`` takes the heating on a regular (lat, lon) grid -- any extent; it is zero outside -- and
returns nondimensional u, v, p on the same grid. The longitude circle is periodic (the whole equator). The
meridional projection uses ``n_modes`` modes, computed by quadrature on the input latitudes (which should
extend a few L_a, i.e. tens of degrees, from the equator for accurate projections; Q outside them is zero).

methods.name: project
methods.doc: Mode coefficients Q_n(x) (..., n_modes + 2, nlon) of Q (..., nlat, nlon) on the circle.

methods.name: solve_modes
methods.doc: Fourier coefficients of q_n and v_n from heating modes Qn (..., N+2, nlon).

methods.name: solve
methods.sig: (Q: np.ndarray, lat: np.ndarray, lon: np.ndarray, out_lat: np.ndarray | None = None) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]
methods.doc:
Response to Q (..., nlat, nlon_in) given at longitudes ``lon`` (a subset of the circle at spacing
``dlon``); fields returned at ``out_lat`` (default ``lat``) on the input longitudes.

classes.name: CoupledParams
classes.doc: Parameters of :class:`CoupledModel` (SST coefficients per ocean-grid longitude, in months).

classes.name: CoupledModel
classes.sig: (params: CoupledParams, ocean: ShallowWaterOcean | None = None, atmosphere: GillAtmosphere | None = None, dt_hours: float = 8.0, atm_every: int = 3, closure: Callable | None = None, atm_lat: float = 40.0)
classes.doc:
Linear coupled ocean-atmosphere anomaly model on :class:`OceanGrid`; time in months for the SST equation
and seconds inside the ocean step. ``closure(T, h)`` (optional) adds a learned SST tendency [K/month] -- the
hybrid models train it.

methods.name: gill_winds
methods.doc: Nondimensional Gill u at u points and v at v points (ocean grid) for heating Q = T (K).

methods.name: operator
methods.doc:
The Gill map T -> (u at u points, v at v points) as a truncated SVD (it is linear): applied to every
unit SST anomaly once, then kept to the singular values above ``tol`` times the largest (or ``rank``).
Cached in memory per model and on disk per (grid, eps, c_a, modes, tol).

methods.name: run
methods.sig: (state, n_months: int, *, T_obs: np.ndarray | None = None, nudge_days: float = 5.0, tau_ext: Callable | None = None, seed: int = 0, record: bool = True, stochastic: bool | None = None, noise_scale: np.ndarray | float = 1.0)
methods.doc: Integrate ``n_months`` from ``state`` (dict of u, v, h, T arrays with a common batch shape).

functions.name: gill_analytic
functions.sig: (x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, L: float, eps: float, period: float) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]
functions.doc:
Closed-form long-wave Gill response on a periodic circle of length ``period`` (Matsuno units) to
Q = F(x) exp(-y^2 / 2) with F = cos(pi x / (2 L)) for |x| < L, else 0. Kelvin part q0 = -int G_K(x - s) F(s) ds,
Rossby part q2 = -1/2 int G_R(s - x) F(s) ds with the periodic Green's functions
G(d) = exp(-a d) / (1 - exp(-a P)), a = eps (Kelvin), 3 eps (Rossby), d in [0, P).

functions.name: sst_tendency
functions.sig: (T, h, taux_c, eps_T, gamma, kappa, S)
functions.doc:
dT/dt [K/month] = -eps_T T + gamma S h + kappa S tau_x (T, h, tau_x at cell centres; gamma, kappa per
longitude; S the meridional structure (ny, 1)).

functions.name: kelvin_wave_test
functions.sig: (grid: OceanGrid | None = None, c: float = 2.7, dt_hours: float = 6.0, days: float = 40.0, sigma_km: float = 1500.0) -> dict
functions.doc:
Release an equatorial Kelvin wave (h = exp(-y^2 / 2 L^2 - (x - x0)^2 / 2 s^2), u = g' h / c, v = 0) in the
western basin without damping; its speed is the slope of the tracked equatorial h peak. Theory: c; basin
crossing time = basin width / c.

functions.name: rossby_wave_test
functions.sig: (grid: OceanGrid | None = None, c: float = 2.7, dt_hours: float = 6.0, days: float = 150.0, sigma_km: float = 2500.0) -> dict
functions.doc:
Release a long n = 1 Rossby wave (Matsuno structure u ~ (2 y^2 - 3), h ~ (2 y^2 + 1) times exp(-y^2 / 2)
in units of L = sqrt(c / beta)) in the eastern basin; its h centroid moves west at c / 3 in the long-wave
limit (finite width makes it slightly slower).

functions.name: gill_test
functions.sig: (nlons = (72, 144, 288, 576), eps: float = 0.1, L: float = 2.0, n_modes: int = 12) -> dict
functions.doc:
Numerical Gill response to Q = cos(pi x / 2L) exp(-y^2 / 2) on |x| < L against :func:`gill_analytic`, for
several longitude resolutions (relative L2 error of u, v, p over the band |y| < 3).

functions.name: convergence_study
functions.sig: (factors = (1, 2, 4), c: float = 2.7) -> dict
functions.doc:
Kelvin-wave speed error under joint refinement of dx, dy and dt (factor f: dlon = 5/f deg, dlat = 2/f deg,
dt = 12/f h).

functions.name: forced_ocean_run
functions.sig: (ocean: ShallowWaterOcean, taux: np.ndarray, *, steps_per_month: int = 91, tauy: np.ndarray | None = None, state: dict | None = None) -> tuple[np.ndarray, dict]
functions.doc:
Integrate the ocean alone under prescribed monthly stress ``taux`` (months, ny, nx + 1) [N m-2] (and ``tauy``
at v points); returns the monthly mean h (months, ny, nx) and the final state. NaN stress months are zero.

children.name: pinneapple_systems.time_series.enso.oscillators
children.doc:
Conceptual ENSO models: the recharge oscillator and the delayed oscillator.

**Recharge oscillator** (Jin 1997, J. Atmos. Sci. 54:811; the linear stochastic form of Burgers et al. 2005, GRL
32:L13706 and Jin et al. 2020, in *El Nino Southern Oscillation in a Changing Climate*, AGU), with T the eastern
Pacific SST anomaly [K] and h the warm-water-volume / thermocline-depth anomaly [m], t in months::

    dT/dt = R(s) T + F1(s) h + sigma_T (1 + B T) xi_T
    dh/dt = -F2(s) T - eps(s) h + sigma_h xi_h

Each coefficient may carry an annual cycle c(s) = c0 + c1 cos(2 pi s / 12) + c2 sin(2 pi s / 12) of the calendar
month s (0 = January); the seasonal growth rate R(s) is the textbook origin of the spring predictability barrier
(Stein et al. 2014, J. Climate 27:4985). B != 0 is multiplicative (state-dependent) noise (Levine & Jin 2017, Clim.
Dyn. 48:3241 discuss its role in ENSO asymmetry). The constant-coefficient system has eigenvalues
``lambda = (R - eps) / 2 +- sqrt((R + eps)^2 / 4 - F1 F2)`` (:func:`ro_eigen`): growth rate (R - eps) / 2 and,
when F1 F2 > (R + eps)^2 / 4, period 2 pi / sqrt(F1 F2 - (R + eps)^2 / 4).

Parameters are estimated (:func:`fit_recharge`) by least squares of the centred monthly tendencies on the state
(times the annual harmonics), the method of the extended recharge oscillator of Zhao et al. (2024, Nature 630:891);
the noise amplitudes from the residuals, B by maximum likelihood of the T residuals.

**Delayed oscillator** (Suarez & Schopf 1988, J. Atmos. Sci. 45:3283; Battisti & Hirst 1989, J. Atmos. Sci.
46:1687)::

    dT/dt = a T - b T(t - tau) - c T^3

linearised roots ``lambda = a + W_k(-b tau exp(-a tau)) / tau`` (Lambert W, :func:`do_roots`).

classes.name: ROParams
classes.doc:
Recharge-oscillator coefficients per month: ``coef[name] = (c0, c1, c2)`` (annual harmonics; c1 = c2 = 0 for a
constant coefficient), noise amplitudes per sqrt(month), multiplicative noise B [1/K].

methods.name: constant
methods.sig: (R: float, F1: float, F2: float, eps: float, **kw) -> ROParams

functions.name: ro_eigen
functions.sig: (R: float, F1: float, F2: float, eps: float) -> dict[str, float]
functions.doc:
Eigenvalues of the constant-coefficient recharge oscillator: growth rate [1/month], period [months] (inf
when the eigenvalues are real) and the two eigenvalues.

functions.name: ro_coefficients
functions.sig: (p: ROParams, month: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]
functions.doc: Coefficients at (fractional) calendar month(s) ``month`` (0 = mid-January... any real number, period 12).

functions.name: ro_tendency
functions.sig: (p: ROParams, X: np.ndarray, month) -> np.ndarray
functions.doc: Deterministic tendency (dT/dt, dh/dt) of states X (..., 2) at calendar month(s) ``month``.

functions.name: simulate_recharge
functions.sig: (p: ROParams, x0, n_months: int, *, month0: float = 0.0, sub: int = 10, n_members: int = 1, stochastic: bool = True, seed: int = 0, method: str = 'rk4', month_offsets: np.ndarray | None = None) -> np.ndarray
functions.doc:
Integrate from x0 ((2,) or (n, 2) states) for ``n_months``; returns (n_members, n, n_months + 1, 2) samples at
month ends. Deterministic part: RK4 (``method="rk4"``) or Euler; noise: Euler-Maruyama with ``sub`` steps per
month (Ito; the multiplicative factor is clipped at zero). ``month_offsets`` (n,) gives each state its own start
month (added to ``month0``).

functions.name: fit_recharge
functions.sig: (T: np.ndarray, h: np.ndarray, month: np.ndarray | None = None, *, seasonal: Sequence[str] = (), multiplicative: bool = False, lead: int = 1, sub: int = 4) -> ROParams
functions.doc:
Recharge oscillator fitted to monthly series T, h (pairs with a NaN are skipped).

The drift is estimated by least squares of ``lead``-month predictions of the integrated model (RK4, ``sub``
steps per month) from every observed state, each variable scaled by its standard deviation -- for a linear SDE
the conditional mean is the deterministic flow, so this is unbiased where a regression of finite-difference
tendencies on the state is not (a centred difference correlates with the noise). The start is the matrix
logarithm of the one-month propagator C(1) C(0)^-1 (the linear inverse model estimate). Coefficients named in
``seasonal`` get annual harmonics of the calendar month (0-11). Noise: the standard deviation of the one-month
residuals (the diffusion over one month, neglecting the drift's effect within the month); with
``multiplicative`` the factor (1 + B T) of the T noise by maximum likelihood.

functions.name: do_rhs
functions.sig: (x, xt, a: float = 1.0, b: float = 0.75, c: float = 1.0)
functions.doc: Battisti-Hirst / Suarez-Schopf delayed oscillator dT/dt = a T - b T(t - tau) - c T^3.

functions.name: do_roots
functions.sig: (a: float, b: float, tau: float, branches: Sequence[int] = (0, -1, 1)) -> list[complex]
functions.doc:
Roots of the linear characteristic equation lambda = a - b exp(-lambda tau) on Lambert-W ``branches``,
sorted by decreasing real part.

functions.name: simulate_delayed
functions.sig: (a: float, b: float, c: float, tau: float, history, n_steps: int, dt: float, method: str = 'rk4') -> np.ndarray
functions.doc:
Method of steps on a uniform grid (``tau`` a multiple of ``dt``): ``history`` holds the last tau / dt + 1
values (oldest first); returns the n_steps new values. RK4 uses the mean of the delayed values at the half step
(second order in the delayed argument) unless the grid is refined.

functions.name: oscillation_stats
functions.sig: (x: np.ndarray, dt: float, *, skip: int = 0) -> dict[str, float]
functions.doc:
Period (mean spacing of upward zero crossings, linearly interpolated) and growth rate (slope of log |peak|
over successive extrema) of a linear oscillation sampled every ``dt``.

children.summary: Conceptual ENSO models: the recharge oscillator and the delayed oscillator.

children.name: pinneapple_systems.time_series.enso.pinn
children.doc:
Physics-informed networks for ENSO, trained with :class:`pinneapple_neural.trainer.inverse_pinn.InversePINN`
(network weights and unknown physical parameters optimised together; data misfit plus ODE/PDE residual at random
collocation points, adaptive weighting).

* :func:`identify_recharge` -- a PINN for the recharge oscillator on a stretch of observed (T, h): the network
  X(t) fits the data while dX/dt - f(X; theta) is penalised; theta = (R, F1, F2, eps) (optionally seasonal) is
  learned, and an optional neural closure g(h) of the thermocline feedback is added to dT/dt.
  :class:`PINNRechargeForecaster` forecasts by integrating the identified equations from the observed state.
* :class:`PINNExtrapolationForecaster` -- the "PINN as a forecaster" test: for every origin a PINN is fitted to
  the last ``window`` months and to the recharge-oscillator residual on [origin - window, origin + max(h)]; the
  forecast is the network beyond the data. One grouped network (independent weights per origin) trains all origins
  at once.
* :class:`EquatorialWavePINN` -- a PINN for the long-wave shallow-water equations projected on the equatorial
  Kelvin and first-meridional Rossby modes (the two-mode reduction of the linear model in :mod:`.intermediate`)::

      dq0/dt + c dq0/dx + r q0 = s X0                   q = g' h / c + u  (Matsuno variables, m/s)
      dq2/dt - c/3 dq2/dx + r q2 = s (2 X2 - X0) / 6     X_n = projections of tau_x / (rho H) on phi_n(y / L)
      h(x, 0, t) = (H / c) (q0 / 2 + q2)                 east wall: q2 = q0 / 2 (no net zonal mass flux)
                                                          west wall: q0 = a_W q2 (a_W = 2: closed, < 2: leaky)

  coupled to an equatorial SST equation dT/dt = -eps_T T + kappa tau_x + g_NN(x, h) whose thermocline-feedback
  closure g_NN is learned. Data: observed equatorial D20 and SST anomalies; forcing: ERA5 stress. Unknowns: c, r,
  a_W, the forcing scale s, eps_T, kappa and the closure.

classes.name: FourierMLP
classes.sig: (in_dim: int, out_dim: int, hidden: int = 64, layers: int = 3, n_freq: int = 8, out_scale: Sequence[float] | None = None, freq_max: float | None = None)
classes.doc:
MLP on [x, sin(2 pi k x_j), cos(2 pi k x_j)] (k = 1..n_freq for each input j, inputs scaled to [0, 1]),
tanh hidden layers; ``out_scale`` multiplies the outputs.

classes.name: GroupedMLP
classes.sig: (groups: int, in_dim: int, out_dim: int, hidden: int = 32, layers: int = 2, n_freq: int = 4, freq_max: float = 2.0, out_scale: Sequence[float] | None = None, seed: int = 0)
classes.doc: G independent Fourier MLPs evaluated on the same inputs: (B, in) -> (B, G * out) (group-major).

classes.name: PINNRechargeForecaster
classes.sig: (h_col: str = 'wwv', seasonal: Sequence[str] = (), closure: bool = False, stochastic: bool = False, n_members: int = 200, epochs: int = 4000, seed: int = 0, name: str | None = None, family: str | None = None)
classes.doc:
Forecasts by integrating the recharge oscillator identified by :func:`identify_recharge` on the training
segment (``closure``: with the learned thermocline-feedback network). ``stochastic``: ensemble with the noise
of the one-month residuals; otherwise deterministic with a calibrated Gaussian spread.

classes.name: PINNExtrapolationForecaster
classes.sig: (h_col: str = 'wwv', window: int = 24, epochs: int = 3000, n_col: int = 512, hidden: int = 32, chunk: int = 256, seed: int = 0, name: str | None = None)
classes.doc:
For each origin t: a PINN X(tau), tau = (s - t) / window in [-1, max(h) / window], fitted to the observed
(T, h) of the last ``window`` months and to the recharge-oscillator residual (coefficients fitted by least
squares on the training segment, held fixed) on the whole interval; the forecast at t + h is X(h / window).
All origins of a call train together as one :class:`GroupedMLP` (chunks of ``chunk``).

classes.name: EquatorialWavePINN
classes.sig: (lon_obs, h_obs, T_obs, lon_f, X0, X2, tau_eq, *, lon_w: float = 120.0, lon_e: float = 280.0, H: float = 150.0, sst: bool = True, c0: float = 2.0, r0_days: float = 365.0, hidden: int = 96, layers: int = 4, n_freq: int = 12, freq_max: float | None = None, learn: Sequence[str] = ('c', 'r_T', 'a_W'), fixed: dict[str, float] | None = None, pde_weight: float = 1.0, seed: int = 0)
classes.doc:
PINN for the two-mode long-wave equatorial ocean plus an equatorial SST equation (see the module docstring).

``lon_obs`` (nb,) and ``months`` define the observation grid of ``h_obs`` and ``T_obs`` (nt, nb) [m, K];
``X0``, ``X2`` (nt, nx) and ``tau_eq`` (nt, nx) are the projected forcing and the equatorial stress on
``lon_f``; the basin spans [lon_w, lon_e]. ``sst=False`` fits the ocean only (h data).

methods.name: fit
methods.sig: (epochs: int = 6000, n_col: int = 4096, lr: float = 0.002) -> dict[str, Any]
methods.doc:
Train; returns the identified parameters, the residual RMS of each equation on 8192 fresh points (in
units of the typical tendency), and the data RMSE and correlation.

methods.name: closure_curve
methods.doc: The learned thermocline-feedback tendency g(x, h) [K/month] at longitude ``lon`` for D20 anomalies h.

methods.name: predict_grid
methods.sig: (lon: np.ndarray, n_t: int | None = None) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]
methods.doc: h (D20-equivalent, m) and T (K) on (months, lon) for the fitted window.

functions.name: identify_recharge
functions.sig: (T: np.ndarray, h: np.ndarray, month: np.ndarray | None = None, *, seasonal: Sequence[str] = (), closure: bool = False, epochs: int = 4000, n_col: int = 2048, hidden: int = 64, layers: int = 3, n_freq: int = 32, lr: float = 0.002, seed: int = 0, init: O.ROParams | None = None, freq_period: float = 6.0) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
PINN identification of the recharge oscillator on monthly series (T, h) of length n.

Time is scaled to s = t / n in [0, 1]; the network outputs (T, h) in data units; the residual of each equation
is divided by that variable's standard deviation (per month). Learned: R, eps (free sign), F1, F2 (positive,
log-space), annual harmonics of the coefficients in ``seasonal``, and with ``closure`` a 1-16-16-1 network
g(h / sd_h) * sd_T added to dT/dt (its last layer starts at zero). ``init`` gives starting values (default:
R = -0.05, F1 = 0.02 sd_T / sd_h, F2 = 1.5 sd_h / sd_T, eps = 0.03, which is not the answer).

Returns the identified :class:`~.oscillators.ROParams` (noise from one-month integrated residuals), the data
RMSE per variable, the residual RMS on 4096 fresh collocation points, the history, and the trained modules.

functions.name: project_forcing
functions.sig: (taux: np.ndarray, lat: np.ndarray, c: float = 2.7, H: float = 150.0, rho: float = 1025.0) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]
functions.doc:
Projections X0, X2 of X = tau_x / (rho H) [m s-2] (..., nlat, nx) on phi_0 = exp(-y^2/2) and
phi_2 = (4 y^2 - 2) exp(-y^2/2), y = lat / L with L = sqrt(c / beta) (norms sqrt(pi) and 8 sqrt(pi)).

Returns
-------
X0 : np.ndarray [m/s2]
    Projection on phi_0.
X2 : np.ndarray [m/s2]
    Projection on phi_2.

children.name: pinneapple_systems.time_series.enso.pipeline
children.doc:
Study-level steps of the ENSO study, each returning JSON-able results (the example script only calls these).

* :func:`solver_checks` -- every solver against theory (Kelvin / Rossby speeds and crossing times, convergence,
  Gill vs closed form, recharge oscillator vs eigenvalues for several time steps, delayed oscillator vs its root).
* :func:`enso_scores` -- ACC per lead, skill by target month, categorical scores for every model of a merged zoo.
* :func:`case_panels` -- plume data (quantiles at the evaluated leads) for the case-study origins.
* :func:`spring_barrier_hindcasts` -- blocked cross-validated hindcasts of cheap models over the development
  period (more forecasts per target month than the test period has).
* :func:`phase_portrait` -- observed (h, T) and the fitted recharge oscillators' paths and realisations.
* :func:`shallow_water_pinn_study` -- the equatorial-wave PINN on synthetic data from the 2-D model (known c, r)
  and on the observations of a window, with the Hovmoller fields of observations, the ERA5-forced 2-D ocean and
  the PINN.
* :func:`slab_frames` -- monthly SST and thermocline-depth fields for the 3-D render of an event.
* :func:`markdown_tables` -- the guide's tables from the stored results.

functions.name: solver_checks
functions.sig: () -> dict[str, Any]

functions.name: enso_scores
functions.sig: (merged: dict[str, Any], month_of_year: np.ndarray, threshold: float = 0.5) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc: ACC per lead, target-month stratified ACC / RMSE and categorical scores of every model in ``merged``.

functions.name: case_panels
functions.sig: (parts: dict[str, dict], merged: dict[str, Any], data, *, families = ('physical', 'hybrid', 'data', 'data+physics'), events: dict[str, Any] | None = None, months_before: int = 18, leads: Sequence[int] = (1, 3, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24)) -> list[dict]
functions.doc:
Plume panels: for every case-study origin, the representative of each family (from ``merged``) with its
quantiles at the evaluated leads. ``parts[name]["_cases"]`` holds forecasts from origins after the development
period; ``events[label][name]`` (from :func:`.study.event_hindcast`) those of refitted models.

Each panel's ``sample`` says whether the forecasts are out of sample and why: "test period", "after the test
period", "refit: data to <month>" (an event refit; no data after that month entered the fit) or "in-sample
(training period)" (a model fitted on data that include the target years); the title carries it.

functions.name: skill_against
functions.sig: (merged: dict[str, Any], reference: str = 'climatology', alpha: float = 0.05) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
RMSE skill 1 - RMSE / RMSE(reference) on the test period for every model of ``merged`` (with its kept
forecasts), and one-sided Diebold-Mariano tests (squared errors, HLN, long-run variance over the h-step
overlap) of each non-baseline model against the reference, Holm-adjusted across those models at each lead.

functions.name: spring_barrier_hindcasts
functions.sig: (data, prot, makers: dict[str, Any], *, block: int = 48) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
Blocked, purged cross-validated hindcasts over the development period for each maker; returns, per model,
the target-month stratified ACC / RMSE and the ACC per lead.

functions.name: phase_portrait
functions.sig: (data, prot, *, seasonal = ('R', 'F1', 'F2', 'eps'), seed: int = 0, onsets: Sequence[str] = ('1997-04', '2009-06', '2015-03', '2023-04'), n_path: int = 48) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
Observed (h, T) over the record (and its 3-month running mean), the deterministic paths of the fitted
recharge oscillators (constant and seasonal) for ``n_path`` months from the observed state at each El Nino
onset in ``onsets``, and one stochastic realisation of each with the record's length; parameters fitted on the
training segment.

functions.name: shallow_water_pinn_study
functions.sig: (ds, window: tuple[str, str] = ('1996-01', '1999-12'), *, epochs: int = 6000, n_col: int = 4096, pde_weight: float = 100.0, spin_months: int = 36, seed: int = 0) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
The equatorial-wave PINN (:class:`.pinn.EquatorialWavePINN`) on (a) synthetic equatorial h from the 2-D
shallow-water model forced by ERA5 stress (known c = 2.7 m/s, r = 1/900 d, closed west wall) and (b) observed
2S-2N D20 and SST anomalies, both over ``window``; plus the Hovmoller fields (observed, the ERA5-forced 2-D
model scaled by its fitted amplitude factor, the PINN).

functions.name: slab_frames
functions.sig: (ds, oisst, casts, start: str, end: str, *, spin_months: int = 36, lon = (121.0, 279.0), lat = (-19.5, 19.5)) -> list[dict]
functions.doc:
Monthly frames for :func:`.render.render_frames`: full SST [deg C] from OISST (1 deg) and thermocline depth
= the D20 climatology of the casts (2 deg lat x 10 deg lon bins, base period, smoothed and interpolated to
the SST grid) plus the anomaly of the ERA5-forced 2-D ocean model, scaled to D20 by its fitted factor.

functions.name: markdown_tables
functions.sig: (res: dict[str, Any], leads: Sequence[int] = (1, 3, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24)) -> dict[str, str]
functions.doc: Markdown tables of the study from the stored results (``res``: the study JSON).

children.name: pinneapple_systems.time_series.enso.plots
children.doc:
Figures of the ENSO study, in the style of :mod:`pinneapple_systems.time_series.forecast_lab.plots` (same family
colours, grid and spines): forecast plumes, skill against lead, the spring-barrier heatmap, the recharge-oscillator
phase portrait and Hovmoller diagrams.

functions.name: plot_plumes
functions.sig: (panels: list[dict], path: str, *, ncols: int = 3) -> str
functions.doc:
Forecast distributions at the evaluated leads from one origin per panel, one family per colour (median
marker, 50 % thick and 90 % thin interval bars, slightly offset per family), observed Nino 3.4 in black.
Each panel: ``title``, ``t_obs``/``y_obs`` (months as fractional years), ``origin_t``, and ``fams``: list of
{family, name, t (lead times), q (5 x n quantiles 5/25/50/75/95 %)}.

functions.name: plot_skill_vs_lead
functions.sig: (curves: dict[str, dict], path: str, *, metrics = ('acc', 'rmse_skill_vs_best_baseline'), labels: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> str
functions.doc:
One panel per metric: each curve (``family``, ``horizons``, values, optional ``significant`` mask) against
lead; baselines dashed grey.

functions.name: plot_spring_barrier
functions.sig: (maps: dict[str, dict], path: str, *, ncols: int = 3, key: str = 'acc') -> str
functions.doc:
Heatmaps of ``key`` (ACC) by target month (rows) and lead (columns), one per model; cells with too few
forecasts are blank, the count range is in each title.

functions.name: plot_phase_portrait
functions.sig: (traj: dict[str, dict], path: str) -> str
functions.doc:
(h, T) phase portraits: ``traj[name] = {"h", "T", "family" or "color", "lw", "alpha"}``; arrows show the
direction of time on the first (observed) curve.

functions.name: plot_hovmoller
functions.sig: (panels: list[dict], path: str, *, ncols: int = 3) -> str
functions.doc:
Hovmoller diagrams (longitude x time): each panel ``title``, ``lon``, ``t`` (fractional years), ``z`` (nt,
nlon), ``vmax``, ``units``.

functions.name: plot_validation
functions.sig: (kelvin: dict, gill: dict, conv: dict, ro: dict, path: str) -> str
functions.doc:
Solver checks: Kelvin-wave speed error under refinement, Gill error against resolution, recharge-oscillator
period and growth (numerical vs analytic) against the time step.

children.summary: Figures of the ENSO study, in the style of pinneapple_systems.time_series.forecast_lab.plots (same family colours, grid and spines): forecast plumes, skill against lead, the spring-barrier heatmap, ...

children.name: pinneapple_systems.time_series.enso.render
children.doc:
3-D renders of the tropical Pacific during an ENSO event with the library's Blender Cycles renderer
(:func:`pinneapple_tools.visualization.studio.render`).

:func:`slab_scene` builds a cut-away slab of the basin: the sea surface coloured by SST from 2S to 20N, a vertical
wall along 2S from the surface down to the thermocline coloured by the SST of that row, and the 20 deg C isotherm
(thermocline) surface over the whole width below, coloured by its depth anomaly on a diverging scale with its own
colour bar -- so the warm-water layer's thickness, the thermocline tilt and the eastward shift of warm water during
El Nino are visible together. Depths are exaggerated (``z_per_100m``).
:func:`render_frames` renders a sequence of months (optionally interpolated in time) with a date label, and
:func:`encode_video` writes an H.264 MP4 with ffmpeg.

functions.name: slab_scene
functions.sig: (lon: np.ndarray, lat: np.ndarray, sst: np.ndarray, d20: np.ndarray, *, d20_anom: np.ndarray | None = None, band_deg: float = 2.0, z_per_100m: float = 1.0, x_per_deg: float = 0.06, y_per_deg: float = 0.12, floor_m: float = 300.0, title: str = '')
functions.doc:
Scene of SST [deg C] (ny, nx) and thermocline depth ``d20`` [m, positive down] (ny, nx) on the same
(lat, lon) grid (lon 0-360). The sea surface north of ``band_deg`` N and the equatorial band (``band_deg`` S
to N) carry ``sst``; the band's southern wall drops from the surface to the thermocline and carries the SST of
that row; ``d20_anom`` [m] (optional) is the thermocline surface's field ``dz``. NaN SST (land) is drawn at the
field's minimum; NaN depth takes its row mean.

functions.name: render_frames
functions.sig: (frames: Sequence[dict], out_dir: str, *, sst_range: tuple[float, float] = (22.0, 31.0), size: tuple[int, int] = (960, 540), samples: int = 24, view = (-0.4, -1.0, 0.75), interpolate: int = 1, dz_range: float = 40.0, **scene_kw) -> list[str]
functions.doc:
Render ``frames`` (dicts with ``lon``, ``lat``, ``sst``, ``d20``, optionally ``d20_anom``, and a ``label``)
to PNG files in
``out_dir``; ``interpolate`` > 1 inserts linearly interpolated frames between consecutive months. Needs
``bpy`` (``pip install bpy``) or a run inside Blender.

functions.name: encode_video
functions.sig: (paths: Sequence[str], out: str, fps: int = 8, crf: int = 30) -> str
functions.doc: H.264 MP4 (yuv420p, even frame size) from PNG frames with ffmpeg.

children.summary: 3-D renders of the tropical Pacific during an ENSO event with the library's Blender Cycles renderer (pinneapple_tools.visualization.studio.render).

children.name: pinneapple_systems.time_series.enso.study
children.doc:
The ENSO forecasting study: the protocol, the model zoo, and one call per model (so the zoo runs in parallel
processes and is merged by :func:`~pinneapple_systems.time_series.forecast_lab.study.merge_zoo`).

* :func:`protocol` -- horizons 1-12, 15, 18, 21, 24 months; the test period starts at ``test_start`` (default
  2012-01) and is untouched until the final scoring; the last 15 % of the development period is the validation
  block; purged walk-forward tuning on the rest (forecast_lab rules).
* :func:`zoo` -- the specs by family: baselines, data-driven (GBM, MLP, LSTM, TCN, transformer, LIM, CNN),
  data + physics (CNN pre-trained on the intermediate model, PINN-identified recharge oscillator with and without a
  learned closure, PINN extrapolation, MLP with a recharge-oscillator residual loss, GBM with physics features),
  physical (recharge oscillator deterministic / stochastic / seasonal with multiplicative noise, the RO fitted by
  multiple shooting, the delayed oscillator, the intermediate model with SST nudging), hybrid (RO + GBM residual,
  UDE closure of the RO, the intermediate model with EnKF, a multi-model ensemble).
* :func:`run_model` -- tune / fit / score one spec; also the forecasts from the case-study origins.
* :func:`event_hindcast` -- refit a spec on data that end before an event (1997/98) and forecast it.

functions.name: protocol
functions.sig: (months: list[str], test_start: str = '2012-01', horizons = HORIZONS, min_history: int = 36) -> Protocol

functions.name: zoo
functions.sig: (quick: bool = False) -> list[ModelSpec]
functions.doc: The model zoo. ``quick``: tiny epochs / members for smoke runs.

functions.name: spec

functions.sig: (name: str, data: SeriesData, prot: Protocol, *, budget: int = FP.BUDGET, quick: bool = False, case_origins: dict[str, list[str]] | None = None, log: Callable[[str], None] = print, seed: int = 0) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
Tune, fit and score one spec under ``prot`` (forecasts kept for :func:`merge_zoo`), plus its forecasts from
the case-study origins that lie after the development period (``_cases``: label -> origin -> Forecast).

functions.name: event_hindcast
functions.sig: (name: str, data: SeriesData, event_start: str, origins: list[str], *, quick: bool = False, horizons = HORIZONS, min_history: int = 36, val_frac: float = 0.15) -> dict[str, Any]
